title: Signal threshold analysis v1 (PLG → Sales triggers)
content:
TAB: README
Owner: Chris Osei (Product Ops)
Last refresh: 2025-03-07

Purpose
- Analyze historical self-serve Hosted API cohorts to pick high-signal thresholds for a sales-assisted expansion motion (Dedicated/Private).
- Estimate lead volumes (weekly/monthly) at candidate thresholds.
- Document false-positive sampling notes to reduce “spammy” outreach.

Data sources (aggregated)
- Usage windows: 7/14/30d spend, tokens, concurrency, 429 rate-limit hits, model routing failures
- Intent events: pricing page, “Contact sales”, security docs engagement, region/residency docs engagement
- Exclusions: existing opps, CSM-managed enterprise, explicit opt-out, recently contacted (cooldown)

Definitions (working)
- “Self-serve account” = Hosted API only; no Signed Dedicated/Private contract in CRM
- “Company” = billing account domain (best-effort mapping)
- Spend = net billable usage (after free credits); still track gross usage as a separate column
- Concurrency = p95 concurrent in-flight requests (or equivalent proxy) measured on /chat/completions and /embeddings

Time range used for analysis
- Cohort window: 2024-12-01 → 2025-02-20 (81 days)
- Sampling window for false positives: last 30 days of the cohort window

Notes
- Volumes below assume gating + dedupe applied (see Lead volume estimates tab).
- v1 goal: low false positives, fewer triggers, make playbook easy. v1.1 can add more nuanced signals (e.g., “quality regression / eval failures”).


TAB: Cohorts (historical)
Summary (self-serve population, after basic dedupe of domains)

| Metric | Value | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Total self-serve companies observed (>=1 request) | 4,862 | includes free + paid |
| Paid self-serve companies (gross spend > $0) | 1,174 | may be mostly free-credit usage early |
| Paid self-serve companies (net spend > $50) | 612 | removes most “toy” usage |
| Companies with >= 1 “high intent” event | 338 | pricing page repeat, contact sales, security docs |
| Companies with >= 5 days active in last 14d | 742 | activation filter candidate |

Cohort bucketing by spend (net) in trailing 30d

| Spend bucket (30d net) | # companies | % of paid | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| $0–$49 | 562 | 47.9% | lots of free credit + experiments |
| $50–$199 | 274 | 23.3% | many early-stage products |
| $200–$499 | 157 | 13.4% | meaningful production-ish |
| $500–$999 | 88 | 7.5% | often hitting rate limits / throughput issues |
| $1,000–$2,499 | 58 | 4.9% | strong “Dedicated” candidates |
| $2,500+ | 35 | 3.0% | typically needs dedicated capacity / procurement |

Cohort bucketing by p95 concurrency (14d)

| p95 concurrency (14d) | # companies | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| 0–2 | 3,981 | includes inactive accounts |
| 3–10 | 623 | light prod |
| 11–25 | 164 | scaling workloads |
| 26–50 | 63 | likely requires tuning or capacity |
| 51+ | 31 | frequent pain reports + routing failures |

Observed common “pain patterns” from support + call notes (qualitative)
- Rate limiting (429s) appears before spend crosses $1k/mo (often “spiky” usage; could be growth events)
- EMEA accounts disproportionately trigger region/residency docs but many are “research mode” (need better gating)
- Security docs engagement has higher conversion, but volume is lower (good for AE/SE attention)


TAB: Threshold candidates (v1)
Candidate v1 triggers (proposed to ship in pilot)

1) Sustained spend growth (Dedicated motion)
- Rule A: 30d net spend >= $1,500 AND 14d net spend >= $600
- Rule B (alt): 30d net spend >= $2,500 (simple)

2) Rate-limit pain (Dedicated motion)
- Rule A: 429_count_7d >= 200 AND active_days_7d >= 3
- Rule B (alt): 429_count_14d >= 400 AND p95_concurrency_14d >= 20

3) Concurrency spike + latency sensitivity (Dedicated motion)
- Rule A: p95_concurrency_14d >= 35 AND (p95_latency_ms_7d >= 1,200 OR latency_complaint_event = true)
- Rule B (alt): p95_concurrency_7d >= 50 (too spiky; likely noisy)

4) Security intent (Private or Enterprise Hosted / Dedicated)
- Rule A: security_docs_views_14d >= 3 AND unique_days_security_docs_14d >= 2
- Rule B: “Security questionnaire” event fired (explicit)

5) Data residency / region constraint (Private / Dedicated in-region)
- Rule A: residency_docs_views_14d >= 3 AND region = EMEA OR account_country in {DE, FR, NL, SE, UK}
- Rule B: repeated “region not available” errors (telemetry event)

Gating / hygiene (applies to all)
- Must have “company_domain” OR stable billing account id to write to HubSpot company
- Suppression: existing open opportunity OR active customer success-managed enterprise account OR explicit opt-out
- Cooldown: do not re-trigger same company for 14d (unless “contact sales” event)
- Dedupe: one HubSpot task per company per trigger type per cooldown window

Scoring (rough, for prioritization only; not required for v1 workflows)

| Signal | Points | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| 30d net spend >= $2,500 | +6 | strongest predictor of willingness to talk |
| 30d net spend >= $1,500 | +4 | combined with rate limits tends to convert |
| 429_count_7d >= 200 | +3 | requires active_days gating |
| p95_concurrency_14d >= 35 | +3 | better when combined w/ latency |
| Security questionnaire event | +6 | route to AE + SE quickly |
| Security docs engagement (Rule A) | +4 | typically procurement-related |
| Residency docs engagement (Rule A) | +2 | can be “curiosity”; use in combo |
| Contact sales click | +5 | overrides cooldown |


TAB: Lead volume estimates
Assumptions
- “Weekly” = average per week based on last 6 weeks in cohort window
- Suppression removes ~22% of otherwise qualifying accounts (existing opps, enterprise CS-managed, opt-outs)
- Dedupe/cooldown removes ~15% additional (same company qualifying multiple weeks)
- These are directional; pilot will confirm true volumes.

Estimated weekly volumes by trigger (after suppression + cooldown)

| Trigger | Candidate rule | Raw qualifies / week | After suppression | After cooldown | Notes |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Sustained spend growth | 30d >= $1,500 AND 14d >= $600 | 14.2 | 11.1 | 9.4 | manageable for AEs, high value |
| Sustained spend growth (alt) | 30d >= $2,500 | 7.6 | 5.9 | 5.1 | cleaner but lower coverage |
| Rate-limit pain | 429_7d >= 200 AND active_days_7d >= 3 | 19.8 | 15.4 | 13.0 | highest volume; needs good messaging |
| Concurrency + latency | p95_conc_14d >= 35 AND latency pain | 6.2 | 4.8 | 4.0 | likely SE-involved |
| Security intent | security_docs engaged OR questionnaire event | 5.0 | 4.2 | 3.8 | highest conversion expectation |
| Residency intent | residency_docs engaged + EMEA | 4.6 | 3.6 | 3.1 | risk of “research mode” false positives |

Total (if all v1 triggers enabled simultaneously)
- Expected unique companies/week: ~26–34 (because overlap across triggers)
- Expected unique companies/month: ~110–140

Overlap matrix (approx, last 30 days)

| Overlap | Spend growth | 429 pain | Security intent | Residency intent |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Spend growth ∩ 429 pain | 38% |  |  |  |
| 429 pain ∩ Security intent | 9% |  |  |  |
| Security intent ∩ Residency intent | 22% |  |  |  |

Routing impact (capacity check)
- If NA AEs cover ~70% and EMEA ~30%:
  - NA: ~18–24 companies/week
  - EMEA: ~8–10 companies/week
- SDR support recommended for 429 pain to triage + book; AE direct for spend growth + security questionnaire.


TAB: False positive samples
Method
- Pulled 60 companies that qualified for at least one candidate trigger in last 30 days.
- Manual review inputs:
  - HubSpot history: prior contacts, existing opps, notes
  - Support tickets: presence of active incident / already engaged
  - Product telemetry: repeated active days vs one-off spikes
  - Website intent: repeated visits vs single click

High-level findings (60 sample)

| Category | Count | % | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| True positive (sales-worthy now) | 34 | 56.7% | clear pain + ability/willingness |
| Needs nurture (not now, but keep warm) | 15 | 25.0% | early build stage, but real intent |
| False positive | 11 | 18.3% | mostly spiky traffic or internal testing |

Common false positive patterns + mitigations
1) Load tests / benchmark runs
- Pattern: big concurrency for < 1 day, low active_days
- Mitigation: active_days_7d >= 3 gate; or require two-week persistence for concurrency triggers

2) Academic / hobby usage on paid card
- Pattern: medium tokens but no business footprint; no “contact sales”; minimal docs engagement
- Mitigation: require company domain OR “work email” confidence; deprioritize gmail/yahoo domains

3) Residency docs “curiosity clicks” (esp. EMEA)
- Pattern: 1 session reading residency page, no spend, no security actions
- Mitigation: require >=2 unique days or combine with spend/net > $200

4) 429s due to misconfigured retry storm
- Pattern: very high 429_count but low successful tokens; repeated immediate retries
- Mitigation: add ratio check: successful_requests_7d >= 200 OR tokens_7d >= threshold; suggest support playbook first

False positive examples (anonymized notes)
- FP-07: Triggered 429 pain; review showed SDK bug causing retry loop. Account engaged support; outbound would have been redundant. Recommendation: suppression if open support ticket tagged “rate-limit” in last 7d.
- FP-09: Triggered spend growth; was internal Redwood partner demo environment billed to customer domain (known). Recommendation: add “internal/test” allowlist suppressions.

Suggested updates before pilot expansion
- Add support-ticket suppression (if open ticket in last 7d AND already assigned owner)
- Add “active_days” gate to residency and security docs signals (>=2 days)
- Add “successful tokens” minimum for 429 trigger to avoid retry storms


TAB: Segment breakdown
Breakdown of qualifying companies (unique) by region (last 6 weeks)

| Region | % of qualifying | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| NA | 68% | more spend-growth triggers |
| EMEA | 27% | more residency/security intent |
| APAC | 5% | low volume; often region availability questions |

Breakdown by company size band (best-effort enrichment; many unknown)

| Size band | % of qualifying | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| 1–10 | 21% | most “needs nurture” |
| 11–50 | 33% | good SDR motion |
| 51–200 | 24% | strongest Dedicated candidates |
| 201–1000 | 11% | security + procurement heavy |
| 1000+ | 4% | often already in enterprise motion |
| Unknown | 7% | mostly missing domain enrichment |

Breakdown by primary workload (heuristic from endpoints)

| Workload | % of qualifying | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Chat/text generation | 62% | highest 429 + latency complaints |
| Embeddings | 28% | high throughput; Dedicated in-region interest |
| Rerank/other | 10% | smaller but can be strategic |


TAB: Open questions
1) Spend threshold calibration
- Do we want to optimize for (a) conversions or (b) pipeline $ created?
- Proposal: Pilot with spend rule (30d >= $1,500 AND 14d >= $600) for 2 weeks, then evaluate upgrade to $2,500 if SDR load too high.

2) Rate-limit trigger: product vs sales ownership
- For 429 pain, should first touch be support-style “we can help you tune” (SDR + link to docs) vs “talk to sales about Dedicated”?
- Suggestion: first email frames it as “capacity + reliability” consult; if they mention SLAs/residency/procurement, then move to Dedicated/Private talk track.

3) Residency intent signal quality
- Need to distinguish “reading docs” from “blocking requirement.”
- Idea: treat residency docs as low-confidence unless combined with: spend >= $200 OR contact sales OR security docs engaged.

4) HubSpot constraints
- Need confirmation from David Kim (Biz Systems) on which company properties can be written reliably and which are calculated in workflows.
- Ensure “trigger_type”, “trigger_reason”, “window_metrics_snapshot” fields are not too large (watch HubSpot property length limits).

5) KPI tracking
- Define “false positive” operationally: no reply + no meeting + no product engagement change within 21 days? Or SDR disposition?
- Need consistent SDR disposition codes for pilot: {Not a fit, Too early, Already engaged, Interested—booked, Interested—later}.
